How it plays

Online. Quick match is everyone for themselves; Teams 2v2v2 and Teams 3v3 put you in a team with one colour and one land: you claim together, a teammate's land is home, and teammates cannot cut or hurt each other. The team with the most land wins. Whoever is searching for a mode at the same time plays together; computer drivers take the seats nobody took (a match starts when all six seats are taken, 20 seconds after a second player joins, or after 30 seconds alone). One player's device runs each match: if it leaves, another takes over. Practice is you against five computer drivers and needs no connection.

Six craft, three minutes, a small arena: the most land when the clock runs out wins. Fly out of your land and your craft draws a line behind it; come back in to claim everything the line encloses. If a rival crosses your line while you are out, it is cut: the point where it was crossed lights up and a spark races along the line to your craft: 0.7 to 1.3 seconds (longer the more line there is between the cut and you). Back on your own land before it reaches you and you survive (only the line is lost): it is enough only when you are close to home and already heading there. Too late and your craft goes up. GET HOME at the top of the screen counts the seconds, and an arrow round your craft points to your nearest land. A destroyed craft comes back in a moment on free ground, not inside anyone's land.

Flying. The craft flies by itself at full speed and never stops. Point the stick where you want to go (it turns sharply: a full turn-round takes about two thirds of a second); let go and it holds its line. After every start it waits for your first touch. BOOST gives a short burst (it recharges). Hold the phone upright or sideways: the game plays both ways.

Pads. Five pads lie on the inner ring, one for each ability, and nothing blocks you: fly straight across them. Hold a pad under your colour to take it: 2 seconds if it is free, 5 to take a rival's (the ring on the pad fills in your colour). Its holder keeps the ability until then and is warned. Be destroyed and you lose your pads at once. A craft holds two pads at most: while you hold two, a free pad under your colour stays free, and a rival's pad you hold for 5 seconds is freed instead of taken.

Missiles two shots: keep a rival in front of you to lock on, then tap. A hit takes half a craft's health: two hits destroy it. A hard turn in its last moment makes a missile miss. Mines three, laid one after another along your path: a mine takes half a craft's health too, so it takes two to destroy one. Shield four seconds: no damage, your line cannot be cut, an EMP does nothing. EMP rivals within 30 m are jammed (no abilities, no boost) and slowed to a third of their speed for about three seconds, and their missiles and mines die. Strike lands 1.3 s after you call it, on a rival's line if one is in front of you: it cuts the line, burns the ground for 14 s (land there is lost and cannot be claimed) and hurts craft in it.

Health and repair. Health does not come back by itself. The green pad in the middle is nobody's: fly across it with less than full health and it restores it all, then recharges for 10 seconds. A craft that comes back after being destroyed has full health.

Ramps (a trial; switch them off under Graphics). Three ramps point at the middle. Fly up one and you are in the air: you cross lines without cutting them, set off no mines, and the line you draw from the air cannot be cut. How far you fly depends on your run-up (fly straight at the ramp: 40 m of straight run-up counts in full) and your speed (a boost goes furthest): from a short hop of about 30 m to about 95 m and 1.3 seconds in the air. A clean launch refills your boost.

Land. There are no walls: land is colour, and anyone can cross it. Destroy a rival, by cutting their line or with a weapon, and all their land becomes yours.

Sound

Sound starts with your first touch. In Safari on an iPhone the silent switch mutes it (the TC World app plays through it). M mutes it on a keyboard.

Keyboard

A and D or the left and right arrows to steer (S or down to ease off), Shift to boost; E missile, Q mines, G shield, V EMP, T strike; C changes the view; M mutes the sound.

  • World Test 15: online play (free for all, 2v2v2 and 3v3, with computer drivers in empty seats), menus, and every match, player and result kept on the server. World Test 14: a far faster picture (a cheaper ground, the Smooth setting straight to the screen on phones, no shader built during play, steady frame pacing at 60 or up to 120 frames a second); sharper turns; ramp jumps by run-up and speed; a cut line burns as a short fuse: close to home you can still make it back; a stronger EMP slow; abilities shown bigger. World Test 13: five abilities on five pads, taken by holding them, two a craft at most; a repair pad (health no longer comes back by itself); a plain colour line for the trail; respawns on free ground; smoother steering; three ramps (a trial); upright and sideways; more announcements. From World Test 12: flat pads, baked colour, relief and roughness textures, a soundtrack, sound effects and an announcer, all made for this game. From World Test 11: hover craft, no barricades, a kill hands you the land. From World Test 10: it flies by itself and you steer. World Test 9's cartoon look: a 240 m arena, toon light and ink outlines; every craft, pad, ramp, plant and cloud is a program written for this game.
  • Rendering: HDR with 4x anti-aliasing, glow, ambient occlusion, depth of field, drifting cloud shadows and a colour grade (High; Medium keeps the glow and the grade; Low is the plain picture).
  • Engine: three.js. Type: Baloo 2 by Ek Type (SIL Open Font License).
